newsitem.title: USA: U.S. oil rig count up in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. oil rig count up in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States increased by three to 918 in the week ended April 4, and stood 193 above the year-ago total of 725, Baker Hughes Inc. said Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by three from a week earlier to 763, while rigs working offshore rose by one to 127.

The number of rigs active in inland waters dropped by one to 28. Among the individual states, the biggest changes was in Louisiana, which was up by 11, Texas, down by six, and California, down by seven.
The Gulf of Mexico rose by one to 122.

A total of 384 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down 17 from last week. The number of rigs searching for natural gas was up by 19 to 533, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at one.
In Canada, the number of working rigs was down 78 at 245 vs. 132 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
